changes: Lowered p1 (Trimalla) confidence to low: the form 'trimallaṃvinā' is garbled, and the stem could be Trimalla or a Sanskrit form of a South Indian name (e.g. Tirumala/Tirumalai).
Added p2 Rāmānuja as author of the root text (Nityārādhanavidhi), given as 'bhāṣyakāra' and named in the closing invocation 'śrīmate rāmānujāya na(maḥ)'.

notes: The commentator's name is corrupt: 'trimallaṃvināviracitaṃ' (fol. 15r10). Possible readings are 'trimallakavinā viracitaṃ' or 'trimallena viracitaṃ', or a Sanskrit form of a Tamil name such as Tirumala/Tirumalai. 'Trimalla' is a best guess. Rāmānuja is the author of the root text (the Nityārādhanavidhi), not of this commentary. He is identified by the epithet 'bhāṣyakāra', and his name also appears in the final invocation 'śrīmate rāmānujāya na(maḥ)', which is cut off. The colophon gives no scribe, date or place.
